IHDP.title: Infant Health and Development Program (semi-synthetic outcomes on real covariates)
IHDP.outcome: yf  (factual cognitive test score); ycf = counterfactual, both SIMULATED
IHDP.ate_true: 4.012 (mu1 - mu0, the KNOWN ground-truth ATE, replication 1)
covariates: x1 (6 continuous: birth weight, head circumference, weeks born pre-term, birth order, neonatal health index, mother's age)
x7..x25 (19 binary: infant sex, twin status, mother's marital status, education, race, cigarette/alcohol/drug use, prenatal care, site 1-8)
IHDP.counterfactuals: ALL -- the file ships ycf (the unobserved arm) AND mu0/mu1 (the noiseless response surfaces), so every unit has both potential outcomes
IHDP.note: Covariates and treatment are REAL (from the 1985-88 RCT); outcomes are simulated from the NPCI 'A' response surface, which is why mu0/mu1 exist. The published benchmark also removes a non-random subset of treated children to induce imbalance.

Twins.title: Twin births, NBER natality 1989-1991, same-sex pairs under 2kg
Twins.treatment: derived: being the HEAVIER twin of the pair (dbirwt_1 > dbirwt_0)
Twins.outcome: mort_0 / mort_1  (1-year mortality of the lighter / heavier twin)
Twins.n_treated: n/a -- BOTH potential outcomes are observed, one per twin
Twins.arm_detail: binary: lighter (0) vs heavier (1) twin of the pair
Twins.counterfactuals: ALL -- mort_0 and mort_1 are both present and non-null on 71345 of 71345 rows (100%), because the pair supplies both arms
Twins.note: Not an RCT. The trick: for a twin PAIR both outcomes are observed, so the pair acts as its own counterfactual and the individual treatment effect is known exactly. Benchmarks then HIDE one twin at random and simulate a confounded assignment.

Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).title: National Supported Work Demonstration, 1975-1979 -- a genuine RCT
Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).treatment: treat  (1 = offered the subsidised-work training programme)
Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).outcome: re78  (real earnings in 1978, US$; the post-treatment year)
Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).naive_bias: $-8498 (swap the RCT controls for CPS controls and the estimate becomes this)
Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).counterfactuals: NONE -- one arm per person; no ycf column exists in the files
Jobs / LaLonde (NSW).note: The canonical test: the RCT gives a trustworthy ATE, then you REPLACE the randomised controls with a survey comparison group (CPS or PSID) and see whether your observational estimator can recover the experimental number.

NHEFS.title: NHANES I Epidemiologic Follow-up Study -- observational, Hernan & Robins textbook
NHEFS.treatment: qsmk  (1 = quit smoking between the 1971 baseline and the 1982 follow-up)
NHEFS.outcome: wt82_71  (weight change in kg, 1971 to 1982). Secondary: death, sbp, dbp
NHEFS.counterfactuals: NONE -- one arm per person, and not even randomised
NHEFS.note: NOT randomised -- people choose to quit. It is the standard worked example for IP-weighting, standardisation and g-methods, so adjustment sets are well documented.

IST.title: International Stroke Trial, 1991-1996 -- a large factorial RCT
IST.treatment: RXASP (aspirin Y/N) and RXHEP (heparin N/L/M) -- a 2 x 3 FACTORIAL randomisation
IST.outcome: OCCODE (1 dead / 2 dependent / 3 not recovered / 4 recovered at 6 months); DEAD14, FDEAD, FRECOVER are binary alternatives
IST.arm_detail: FACTORIAL 2 x 4 = 8 occupied cells. Aspirin Y/N (9720 / 9715) crossed with heparin N / L / M / H (9718 / 4861 / 4611 / 245). H is a small high-dose sub-study; the headline design is usually read as 2 x 3 = 6 arms
IST.note: Randomised, so the raw difference IS the causal effect. The size (~19k patients, 36 countries) and the factorial design make it the usual real-data testbed for heterogeneous-effect and policy-learning methods.

STAR.title: Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio, 1985-1989 -- RCT on class size
STAR.treatment: stark / star1 / star2 / star3  (small | regular | regular+aide, randomised per grade)
STAR.outcome: readk, mathk (and grades 1-3): scaled achievement test scores
STAR.ate_raw: +13.7 points (kindergarten read+math: small class 931.9 minus other 918.2)
STAR.arm_detail: 3 arms per grade, re-recorded each year: small / regular / regular+aide. Kindergarten 1900 / 2194 / 2231 (n=6325); grade 1 1925 / 2584 / 2320 (6829); grade 2 2016 / 2329 / 2495 (6840); grade 3 2174 / 2085 / 2543 (6802)
STAR.counterfactuals: NONE -- one class type per child per year
STAR.note: Randomisation is WITHIN school, so school should be conditioned on. Three treatment arms, not two -- most causal work either drops the aide arm or pools it with regular.
